questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.**

Alarums and Excursion
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2 i.e. confused activity and uproar.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alarums and Excursion **means Frantic activity that causes a clamor
 
• **For example:*** The French armies were not far off, and there were **alarums and excursions** all along the border.*

*​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• The noun **alarum** is an archaic form of alarm, **meaning** a call to arms (the vowel between -r- and -m- in **alarum** perhaps arose from rolling of the -r- in the final syllable of the call).
 
• The noun *excursion* denotes a sortie, i.e. an attack made by troops coming out from a position of defence.
 
• The phrase *alarums and excursions* is an allusion to the frequent collocation of the words *alarum* (also occasionally *alarm*) and *excursion* in stage directions in battle scenes in a number of plays by the English poet and dramatist William Shakespeare (1564-1616)—although neither *alarums and excursions* nor *alarms and excursions* appear in Shakespeare’s plays.

 Types of Conditional Sentences
 Definition and examples
 
 

 Zero conditional Sentence
 
 
It expresses a factual condition.

 Structure: If/When+ present simple+ present simple

 >First Conditional Sentence
 It expresses possible and likely future outcomes.
